events.title: Off Book – Tour de Force (A Force of Tour)
events.summary: Jessica and Zach wrote and composed music for the WGA award-winning Peacock Series Baking It starring Maya Rudolph, Amy Poehler and Andy Samberg. The duo has also written songs and musical sketches for the hit animation show Rick and Morty, Party Over Here (a Fox sketch show produced by The Lonely Island), the Peacock series Pitch Perfect: Bumper In Berlin, Buzzfeed, FunnyOrDie and Nickelodeon. Their improvised musical podcast Off Book has been praised by various online publications including Indie Wire, USA Today, Parade, AV Club and Splitsider and been featured at Comedy Central’s Clusterfest Festival, Moontower, the world renowned Just For Laughs Festival in Montreal, and the Netflix Is A Joke Festival in LA. \n

events.title: AdaMa Quartet: Dances and Traditions Reimagined
events.summary: AdaMa is a newly formed chamber music quartet that brings together a striking blend of strings and winds, four distinct personalities, and stylistic breadth like no other. As the first professional quartet of this instrumentation, this uncommon fusion of clarinet, bass clarinet, violin, and cello allows AdaMa to push boundaries of sonic expression, merging styles and genres, and inspiring new works through targeted commissions and projects.

events.title: Earthwork Music Collective ft. Joe Reilly, Nicholas james Thomasma, Sari Brown
events.summary: Earthwork Music Collective believes in the intrinsic power of music to raise both community and self-awareness. Comprised of musicians, teachers, healers, farmers, water protectors, and community organizers, they encourage cooperation and collaboration, using music as a tool to serve, heal, inspire and empower. Hosted by washboardist-at-large Vince Russo, this monthly series features members from all around MI converging to create cosmic collabs, cultivate lasting relationships with our community, and elevate environmental and social justice movements. This month’s show will feature performances by Joe Reilly, Nicholas James Thomasma, & Sari Brown

events.title: Code Switch: Distributing Blackness, Reprogramming Internet Art
events.summary: Code Switch: Distributing Blackness, Reprogramming Internet Art is a multi-sited exhibition exploring and redefining the history of 'Black data,' centering contributions by artists of African descent to new media art and digital practice. It builds on a historic archival timeline of radical visions from Black makers and brings together contemporary artists to examine the relationship between body and machine in the context of cybercultures and technology.

events.summary: Retired U-M internal medicine professor Joel Howell discusses how physician William Beaumont performed long-range experiments through an opening in a patient he first treated on Mackinac Island in 1822. Second in a series of 4 monthly lectures.
